hook: Voyager 1 went silent 24 billion kilometers away for 48 hours.

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 went silent 24 billion kilometers away for 48 hours.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing Voyager 1 in deep space with a 24 billion kilometer label.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep space ambient hum that suddenly cuts out.
b_roll: NASA artist rendition of Voyager 1 in interstellar space

sections.voiceover: On October 18, 2026, NASA's Deep Space Network failed to detect a signal. But how did the probe survive this blackout while drifting 24 billion kilometers from Earth?
sections.visual_cue: Animation of Earth-based radio dishes scanning an empty void.
b_roll: Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex antenna footage

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 restored contact on its own, yet it loses 4 watts of power every year.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of Voyager 1 probe showing its antenna turning toward Earth.
sections.sfx_cue: A soft, rhythmic digital ping returning.

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 uses radioisotope thermoelectric generators that convert decaying plutonium heat into electricity for survival.
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing internal circuitry and the probe's power decay chart.
b_roll: NASA technical schematics of Voyager power systems

sections.voiceover: A machine launched in 1977 still survives in the dark.
sections.visual_cue: Voyager 1 drifting into the distant starfield.
